Arbitrum.name: Product-Market Fit Before Tokenization
Arbitrum.description: Arbitrum launched mainnet in August 2021 but only introduced its token in March 2023—a gap of 19 months. This allowed the project to demonstrate product-market fit, establish liquidity, and build a live ecosystem before introducing financialization pressures. The token was introduced to decentralize governance, not to fund development.
Arbitrum.author: CIF
Arbitrum.evidenceText: Mainnet live August 31, 2021【History — EV-013】; TGE March 16, 2023【History — EV-024】; airdrop March 23, 2023【History — EV-025】. The 19-month gap shows deliberate sequencing: product first, token second.

Arbitrum.name: Disciplined Treasury Management as a Competitive Advantage
Arbitrum.description: Rather than aggressively spending treasury on growth subsidies, Arbitrum DAO adopted an "institutional capital" approach—diversifying into RWAs, generating yield (~$2.28M), and maintaining a conservative burn rate. This creates long-term sustainability and reduces dependency on token price appreciation.
Arbitrum.author: CIF
Arbitrum.evidenceText: Treasury size $1.21B–$1.3B+; ~93% in ARB, $27.6M in RWAs; ~$2.28M interest generated; "Instead of burning capital for growth, Arbitrum focused on real fee generation"【Phase 5 — Treasury】; "Arbitrum DAO is quietly running one of the most disciplined treasury plays in crypto"【Phase 9 — Financial Decision Pattern】.

Arbitrum.name: Institutional Adoption Requires More Than Marketing
Arbitrum.description: Arbitrum attracted major institutions (Robinhood, BlackRock, Franklin Templeton, LG) through technology readiness, compliance infrastructure, and business development, not through grants or subsidies. Institutions chose Arbitrum because it provided the infrastructure they needed, not because they were paid.
Arbitrum.author: CIF
Arbitrum.evidenceText: Robinhood Chain launched on Arbitrum Orbit with 10% fee share【History — EV-041】; Franklin Templeton, WisdomTree, Spiko deployments【Phase 7 — Applications】; LG Electronics building onchain advertising network; Mastercard expanded stablecoin settlement【Phase 8 — Narrative Position】.

Arbitrum.name: Progressive Decentralization Requires Trade-offs
Arbitrum.description: Arbitrum's path to decentralization is gradual and pragmatic. The Security Council retains emergency powers (freeze funds) to protect users—sacrificing "code is law" purity for practical security. Stage 1 rollup status (January 2026) shows technical progress toward decentralization, but governance remains concentrated among top holders.
Arbitrum.author: CIF
Arbitrum.evidenceText: Security Council froze 30,766 ETH (~$71M) during KelpDAO exploit【History — EV-036】; restraining order from US federal court【History — EV-037】; "sacrificing some decentralization purity to prevent stolen funds from being lost"【Phase 9 — Risk Response Pattern】; Stage 1 rollup status achieved January 2026【Phase 8 — Market Timeline】.

Arbitrum.name: DAO Governance Must Evolve Through Failure
Arbitrum.description: AIP-1 (April 2023) was rejected by DAO because it was too broad and perceived as overreach. This failure led to lasting governance reforms: improved temperature checks, snapshots, vesting requirements, and stricter execution processes. Governance maturity came from learning through failure.
Arbitrum.author: CIF
Arbitrum.evidenceText: AIP-1 proposed 7.5亿 ARB for special grant program【History — EV-027】; rejected with 118M votes against vs 21M for【History — EV-028】; "AIP-1 controversy (2023) led to lasting reforms: improved temperature checks, snapshots, vesting requirements, stricter execution processes"【Phase 9 — Governance Decision Pattern】.

Arbitrum.name: Builder Retention Trumps Builder Attraction
Arbitrum.description: Rather than aggressively recruiting new projects with temporary subsidies, Arbitrum focused on retaining existing builders through technical stability, liquidity depth, and institutional-grade infrastructure. Teams that ship multiple products on Arbitrum and expand (not migrate) demonstrate this principle.
Arbitrum.author: CIF
Arbitrum.evidenceText: "Arbitrum doesn't just attract builders; it keeps them. Teams that ship multiple products on Arbitrum; Protocols that expand instead of migrating; Orbit chains choosing to stay aligned with the stack"【Phase 9 — Ecosystem Decision Pattern】; 1,142 live projects【Phase 8 — Adoption Metrics】.
